Hi Elliotrader,

I am doing good thanks.

I don't know wich TF this is but I want to trade swap from 15min and above.

On your first image, the base looks good to me and the bearish breakout
candle engulfed the previous D. However the move after this bearish
candle is not really strong... So first I'll see if the move down
continues and if there is CP on it's way up for a potential retest. But
like I said, the base looks good.

If this is a HTF, I would zoom in on a LTF to make sure there was no wicks that could have consumed some orders.

The 2nd picture, I do not see upper wicks, so it looks ok. However I
would draw the base from the high to candle close , just a personal
preferance. There is also a bick wick from the doji there, so if price
trades up again, this will be a first potential resistance before coming
 to the base.

Again, if this is a higher TF, I'll look at LTF to see if there are any
retest or wicks already because I prefer FRESH untouched ones....

Also, don't forget to look at your next "area of trouble" before taking
the trade, to make sure that you have enough room to take the trade.

All I said here, is just my way of looking at things, I am not an expert yet, still a student...

Take Care and have a nice weekend too.

Mel

You're welcome, you are right,this is the idea. I added this rule
because sometimes I found myself looking for swap levels where there was
 no obvious base on a HTF but just a break of a previous supply or
demand. So I wanted to remember myself that I want to take a trade from a
 base/cluster. Because if there was a break of a previous s/d and a
base followed by a strong move away then I would know for sure that
demand exceeded supply or vice versa from demand,from this point.
(especially on a HTF)

I like to look at LTF for price action but do not like to trade a LTF s/d area in itself. Will always combine LTF with a HTF...

Mel

Hi Ellotrader,

No problem at all!

Yes, there is a minor spike in this 4h level, you are right, it is in
fact a re-test of a previous demand on a ltf such as a 5min or even
1min. What I liked about the zone, was the strong move away from the
level. I also prefer to trade fresh levels as the probability is always
higher there. Everytime there is a test, the level weakens more and
more. Unfortunately we can never tell for sure if there are still some
orders left or not. So watching the approach can give you some clues
about it.

Hope this helps,

Mel
